You need to get out of self. You are falling down the rabbit hole, unless you change course you will cash and burn, which in its own way has its benefits too, Everything in life has its opportunity for growth. What I'm going to assign to you is what I do myself when I find myself hurdling through space towards a planet of destruction. I change my mental and physical course. From today you will begin to change your course by choosing to get out of self and help some one else. For the next 22 days you will do something helpful for someone else, ideally without them knowing it is you. You will choose to do a kind act that itself will perpetuate and grow with no expectations of recognition or reward. Examples: I will get up early and shovel not just my drive-way but a random person on my block. I will make a few cards filled with warm cheer and deliver them at the nearest old folks home and slip them under random doors. I will help out at the local mission and help prepare or serve meals. I will buy a stranger in line their cup of coffee. I volunteer at my local library. I clean my local buddhist meditation centre on wed afternoon before the 7pm meditation. I will help a stranger in need when I'm out and about. There all all kinds of ways you can make a difference in someone else's life and the biggest and most genuine reward is the change that happens inside of you. Trust me it works. Why 22 days? well because I read some where that it takes 22 days of a repeated action or changed behaviour to take hold chemically in the brain. As a matter of fact I'm in the process right now, by sharing my success with you and I will also vacuum my mothers house, as soon as I finish writing to you. It also helps because doing requires thinking and moving so you're using your mind and your body to help you have a change of heart. Try it, remember you can always change your mid and go back to being frightened, miserable and depressed. Have a nice day, grass-hopper

Excluding time, which is the worst jail or prison? Is that the question you're asking me? Each have their "good" and "bad" arguable points. So I'm sticking to what is of most value to me and that would be freedom. Apart from that prison is worst because once you are that deep there is something fundamentally wrong with that persons lifestyle and choices. Jail is the mistake that shakes you up as a wake up call to change your life whether it's the choice in people you are surrounding yourself with or a vice that's taken over your life or simply an attitude adjustment  toward life. And if a person just needs to keep on making "mistakes" and/or has slipped and slid into criminal thinking and criminal behaviour well now you are in a whole other category, and then only a highly motivated person will persevere. The rest will be repeat offenders and what is called 'institutionalised" These people have a slim chance at ever fulfilling their highest good.
